title: The Psychological Reason You Procrastinate (It's Not Laziness)
script: You're not lazy. You procrastinate because your brain is trying to protect you from emotional discomfort — not physical pain. Psychologists call it 'temporal discounting': your future self feels like a stranger, so why would you suffer now for someone you don't even know? The fix isn't discipline. It's making the task feel less threatening. Break it down to something so small it can't hurt you. Open a document. Write one sentence. That's it. Your brain's threat response calms down the moment you start. And once you're in motion, momentum takes over.
